main_text.l: nim hic quicquam è trivio desumptum
est, aut à vulgari ratione disputandi ; ve-
rum id ipsum, quod ex abditis juris regu-
lis quę in rebus agendis obtinent , [?]eti-
tum est penetralibus. Et licet bene multi,
sparsim nonnulla huc facientia, sun[?]t scri-
ptis inseruerint, quę equidem, vidi, & le-
gi, nec contempsi; nulli tamen, quod sci-
am, universam illam de Jure statutario
materiam, (minime illam ipsam partem,
de quâ maximè laborandum erat), aut
pertractarunt. aut ordine sunt complexi.
Multo minus regulas exhibuerunt, qui-
bus veluti thesibus premissis, multis
hypothesibus, jure consuetudinario, atquė
statutario firmatis, sua constaret ratio.
Quod an meo libello confecero, non e-
quidem velim affirmare; ut qui non i-
gnorem alia multa hactenus à me tradi-
tis, superaddi posse. Sperarę tamen au-
sim, mē viris solidâ juris civilis scientiâ
imbutis, inque praxi hodierna satis exer-
citatis, viam monstrasse, quam forte pl-
anam suâ industriâ planissimam, ac tutissi-
mam sunt redditur[?]. Huic meo instituto
si faveris lector judiciosè, me forte ad
plura & majora proferenda in publicum
instigabis.

page.notes: The first word "nim" is a fragment of "nimirum" or similar, continuing from the previous page. The word after "obtinent" is unclear, probably a word beginning with a long s or P, shown as [?]. "sun[?]t" is a doubtful reading of the word before "scriptis". The final word "redditur[?]" is printed as "reddituri" with a damaged ending. Some words are blurred by show-through and stains; readings were checked against the scan, and the "planam suâ industriâ planissimam" order follows the print.
